pull_requests.author: aimable100
pull_requests.title: core: close four chain-verifier gaps found by the AAT JWS vector suite
pull_requests.body:
Running the AAT draft's JWS vector suite against tenuo-core (transcoded to CBOR warrants) found checks the draft's §7 algorithm requires that the verifier did not perform. None is exploitable alone (signatures and I1 hold), but each is a MUST for an enforcement point and each was a small omission.

**Engine changes**
- I3 issuance ordering: a child may not claim an `issued_at` earlier than its parent (§4.4, §7 step 4j). Added to both DataPlane and Authorizer link checks. Previously only `expires_at` ordering was enforced.
- Root shape for multi-warrant chains: the first element must be a depth-0 warrant with no `parent_hash` (§7 steps 3c/3d). A lone warrant presented by itself is deliberately exempt: Tenuo's wire format allows an intermediate to be presented alone (leaf format) trusted on the anchor's direct signature, and `authorize_one` relies on it. Documented as a profile difference.
- Empty composites: `All`/`Any` with an empty constraints array are rejected as an attenuation in either position (draft -02 §4.5). `All::matches` also rejects an empty conjunction, which would otherwise accept every value. `Any::matches` keeps its deny-all reading, which existing tests rely on.
- Lifetime ceiling: `Authorizer::with_max_token_lifetime` exposes the MAX_TOKEN_LIFETIME check (§7 step 3h) on the public API.

**Conformance test**
`tenuo-core/tests/aat_conformance.rs` transcodes every vector in `ietf/vectors/aat-jws-vectors.json` and asserts its verdict: 58 asserted, 0 disagree, 9 not applicable with stated reasons (typ header, PoP audience, private JWK member, lone-warrant presentation). The allowlist is itself checked against the suite.

**Stacked on #667**, which adds the vector file this test reads. Merge #667 first.

Full tenuo-core suite passes; tenuo-wasm builds; the tenuo-aat vector suite (67) passes against the patched engine.

pull_requests.title: design(protocol): version the MCP authorization envelope
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Design proposal for a versioned `_meta.tenuo` authorization envelope targeted at 0.4.0.

This PR intentionally contains no runtime implementation. It defines the contract and migration invariants first so the proof format receives protocol and security review before code is written.

## Proposed direction

- Treat the unversioned 0.3.2 envelope as legacy v1.
- Add `"version": 2` and bind it cryptographically through the `tenuo-pop-v2` domain.
- Keep 0.3.2 argument canonicalization unchanged in v2.
- Never retry another proof version after signature verification fails.
- Upgrade servers first, then clients, observe legacy traffic, and finally disable v1 by policy.
- Return `unsupported_envelope_version` / `legacy_envelope_disabled` separately from `invalid_pop`.
- Do not restore the 0.3.1 null-stripping proof behavior.

## Review requested

The draft calls out unresolved decisions rather than hiding them:

- reject unknown v2 fields or define an extension container;
- configuration-only rollout versus advisory or mandatory MCP capability discovery;
- duration and default policy for accepting unversioned v1;
- placement of the temporary legacy-emission option;
- whether the equivalent HTTP gateway transport belongs in the same contract;
- whether to include the numeric version in the CBOR challenge as well as the proof domain.

## Validation plan

The proposal requires shared byte-exact Rust/Python/TypeScript vectors, downgrade and no-fallback tests, published-0.3.2 interoperability lanes, rolling-upgrade tests, property tests, and fuzz coverage before implementation is considered complete.

## Relationship to 0.3.2

This is follow-up design work to #771, not part of the 0.3.2 security/correctness release. Version 0.3.2 can retain its documented coordinated-upgrade requirement; this proposal establishes a clean lifecycle for future proof-format changes.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- Documentation-only change; no runtime behavior changed

pull_requests.title: fix(langgraph): let @tenuo_node receive LangGraph config, plus delegation example
pull_requests.body:
Picks up #668 by @yftx293, which adds a local `@tenuo_node` planner → worker delegation example for LangGraph (closes #652). Their original commit is kept as is. Making the example's test pass in CI turned up a real SDK bug, so this PR fixes that as well.

## SDK fix: `@tenuo_node` never received LangGraph's `config`

LangGraph decides whether to pass `config` to a node by calling `inspect.signature(node)`. `@wraps` sets `__wrapped__`, so LangGraph saw the inner `(state, bound_warrant)` signature and never passed `config`. `tenuo_key_id` was silently ignored, and every `@tenuo_node` in a compiled graph bound the `"default"` key. The existing tests missed it because they call the wrapper directly with `config=`.

- The wrapper now advertises `(state, config=None)`, keeping the first parameter's name and annotation so LangGraph still infers the state schema.
- `config` is forwarded only to nodes that declare `config` or `**kwargs`.
- Three new tests in `tests/adapters/test_langgraph.py` run through `compile().invoke()`. All three fail without the fix.

`guard_node` has the same problem. It's tracked in #813 to keep this change small.

## Example
- A separate issuer key mints the root warrant.
- The planner grants the worker `research` only and passes the chain in state.
- The worker binds the child warrant under its own key, and every tool call goes through `enforce_tool_call` with the chain. `publish` is denied and its body never runs.
- `KeyRegistry.reset_instance()` moved out of the example and into the test fixture.

## Test
- The module is registered in `sys.modules` before it runs. That was the Python 3.9 CI failure.
- Coverage for: research allowed and publish never executed, the child narrowed and one level deeper, re-delegation can't recover `publish`, and the planner key comes from config.
- `test_langgraph_tenuo_node.py` + `test_langgraph.py`: 96 passed on 3.14. On 3.9 (LangGraph 0.6.11), all 11 tests for this change pass. `ruff check` and `mypy tenuo/` are clean.

pull_requests.title: feat(python): make observe mode real (enforce | observe; audit/permissive as aliases)
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
`configure(mode="audit")` was a silent no-op. `EnforcementMode`, `TENUO_MODE`, `is_audit_mode()` and `should_block_violation()` all existed, but nothing in the enforcement path read them. This PR wires the mode in once, in the shared layer.

**Modes: `enforce` (default) and `observe`.**
- `observe` is the canonical name, matching Rust's `ObservingGuard`.
- `"audit"` and `"permissive"` are permanent aliases. They work through `EnforcementMode(...)`, `configure(mode=...)` and `TENUO_MODE`.
- `EnforcementMode.AUDIT is EnforcementMode.OBSERVE`.
- New `is_observe_mode()`. `is_audit_mode()` is kept as an alias.

**Where it's wired.** `_apply_observe_mode()` runs on `enforce_tool_call`, `enforce_tool_call_async` and `verify_inbound_call`.
- The full decision still runs.
- A would-deny logs one WARNING, `OBSERVE: would deny <tool>: <reason>`. Its structured `extra=` fields are tool, argument keys, value *type names* (never values), `error_type`, `constraint_violated`, `denial_reason` and `warrant_id`.
- The result comes back `allowed=True, observed=True`, and the denial fields stay populated.
- Integrity failures (bad PoP, untrusted root, expiry) are observed too, with their `error_type` kept. Blocking them would add no security, because in observe mode a call with no warrant proceeds anyway.

**Receipts and control-plane events still record the decision as a deny.** `Runtime.collect_result` and `ControlPlaneClient.emit_for_enforcement` treat `allowed and not observed` as allow.

**Approval gates.** In observe mode there's no prompt. The call is recorded as `error_type="approval_required"` and proceeds, mirroring Rust `WouldRequireApproval`.

**Docs.** The mode sections in `production-guide.md`, `api-reference.md` and `llms.txt` are updated. The `api-reference` import is fixed to `from tenuo.config import EnforcementMode`.

**Every adapter that uses the shared path gets observe mode with no adapter changes.** Adapters with their own pre-checks (CrewAI/OpenAI Tier 1, the A2A no-PoP path) and the ADK/Temporal `dry_run` flags will follow in separate small PRs.

### Behavior changes to note
- **`TENUO_MODE=audit` / `mode="audit"` now actually stops blocking.** It was a no-op before, although the startup warning already claimed violations weren't blocked. Deployments that set it will now really run unenforced.
- `langchain.auto_protect()` defaults to `mode="audit"`, so it now really runs in observe mode, as its docs describe.
- An invalid mode now raises `ConfigurationError` instead of a bare `ValueError`.

### Known limitations / follow-ups
- Observed calls produce **deny** receipts and events, even though the call ran. The receipt schema has no `enforced` / `observed` field yet. Adding one is a follow-up, since it needs a schema change.
- In observe mode, gated calls with no approvals skip the Rust PoP and chain check. The record says "approval required", not what PoP would have found. Approvals that *are* presented are still verified, so an invalid one can still raise.
- `denial_reason` is the core's text, and it may quote an argument value.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/unit/test_observe_mode.py` (21 tests):
  - enforce mode still denies
  - observe mode allows a constraint violation and an unlisted tool, and logs the expected WARNING fields
  - the async path works
  - real allows are untouched
  - the receipt is collected as a deny
  - on the verify path, an invalid PoP is observed with its `error_type` kept
  - the approval gate isn't prompted in observe mode and is still prompted in enforce mode
  - `audit`/`permissive`/`TENUO_MODE` map to observe
  - unknown modes are rejected
- [x] Full Python suite: no new failures compared with main. The remaining failures are pre-existing (MCP SDK 2.x middleware plus flaky property tests on main).
- [x] `ruff check` and `mypy` pass on the changed modules.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.title: fix(cel): bind object arguments as value so optional fields can be tested
pull_requests.body:
For object-valued arguments, `evaluate_with_value_context` bound each field as a top-level CEL variable but not the object itself. Since referencing an absent field is an error, an expression couldn't test whether an optional field was present, and calls that omitted it were denied.

The object is now also bound as `value`, matching how non-object values are already exposed. That allows expressions such as `!has(value.approve) || value.approve == false`. A field named `value` keeps precedence, so existing expressions evaluate the same way. An older verifier treats `value` as an undeclared reference and fails closed.

Tested with two new unit tests in `cel.rs` (optional-field checks, and `value` field precedence) and the existing CEL tests. `cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean. `docs/constraints.md` is updated.

Related: #910 (a first-class optional constraint for top-level arguments).

pull_requests.title: fix(ts): fail closed on empty tool policies, one-use approvals, strict inputs
pull_requests.body:
This tightens how the TypeScript SDK handles empty policies, approvals and unknown options.

**Empty policies**
- `session({ tools })` refuses a tool with `allow: {}` unless the session's own `allow` names that capability. An empty capability in a warrant accepts any arguments, so including one now has to be explicit.

**Approvals**
- `tenuo.tool()` accepts `nonceStore`, with the same shape as the MCP adapter.
- When an allowed call carried approvals, the ones matching the call are consumed before the body runs. Keys come from the signed approval fields, so re-encoding an approval doesn't make it fresh.
- `mcp.verify()` consumes approvals the same way, so a fresh proof-of-possession can't reuse them.

**Stricter inputs (these now throw)**
- Unknown or misspelled keys in tool policies, `session()`, `issue()` and `execute()` options.
- `narrow()` with a lower `minApprovals` than its parent.
- `ttlSeconds: 0`.

**Other changes**
- Adds `Session.toWireString()` for passing a delegated chain as one string.
- `revoke()` errors now carry codes.
- The READMEs match the new behavior, including that a longer child TTL is clamped to the parent's expiry.

**Testing**
- New `core/test/hardening.test.ts` (25 tests) and `mcp/test/approvals.test.ts` (3 tests, real in-memory MCP client and server). They exercise real `execute()`, sessions and approvals, and assert that disallowed tool bodies never run.
- Each fix was mutation-checked.
- core: 347 passed. mcp: 24 passed. Typecheck is clean.

Overlaps with #691 (`noArgs()`) in `client.ts`, `api.ts` and the README. Both sides need to be kept when merging.

pull_requests.title: feat: Optional constraint for optional tool arguments
pull_requests.body:
Adds `Optional(inner)` (constraint type 22, `[22, {"inner": C}]`). A listed argument may be absent; when present it must satisfy `inner`, and it still counts as listed for closed-world checks. Delegation may narrow the inner constraint or make the argument required, but never make a required argument (including `Wildcard`) optional. `Optional` is only valid as the outermost constraint of an argument and is rejected in approval gates. Older verifiers reject warrants that use it, so it fails closed.

A top-level `null` is now treated as absent in the core matcher, so Rust, Python and TypeScript agree: an unlisted null is ignored, and a required argument sent as null is missing. This changes one case: a `Wildcard` argument sent as null was allowed in Rust and TS and is now denied. The spec gains argument-matching (§3.6), CEL variable binding (§3.7) and Optional attenuation (§4.7) sections, and test vector A.19.4.

Bindings: `tenuo.Optional` / `tenuo.OptionalArg` (Python), `optional()` (`@tenuo/core`).

Tested with Rust unit and warrant-level tests, the new vector, Python tests including a LangChain `create_agent` loop, and TS tests through `tool().execute`, `explain()` and `narrow()`.

Stacked on #911. Closes #910.

pull_requests.title: docs: name the two integration modes "constraints only" and "warrants"
pull_requests.body:
Records a vocabulary decision in `CONTRIBUTING.md` so new docs, docstrings and examples use it from now on.

## The decision

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| Tier 1, "Tier 1: Guardrails" | **constraints only** |
| Tier 2 | **warrants** |
| "Tier 1 API" (`configure`, `mint`, `@guard`) | **context API** |
| "Tier 2 API" (`mint_builder`, `grant_builder`, `BoundWarrant`) | **builder API** |

## Why

- **"Tier" meant three things.** Integration modes (`crewai.py`, `autogen.py`, `_builder.py`), core API layers (`config.py`, `constraints.py:232`), and a mitigation level (`constraints.py:412`). The "Tier 1 API" signs warrants, while a "Tier 1" integration does not.
- **"Guardrails" is the category we position against.** The Concepts page compares Tenuo with LLM guardrails.
- **The new names use words the docs already define.** Constraints-only mode really is constraints without a warrant around them, so the upgrade path reads as "wrap your constraints in a warrant". It also makes the task-scoped distinction visible: constraints only applies the same rules for the life of the process, while a warrant follows the task.

## What does not change

`create_tier1_guardrail()`, `create_tier2_guardrail()`, `is_tier2()`, and the `"tier1"` / `"tier2"` values of `AuditEvent.tier` in the OpenAI integration keep their names. Renaming them is an API change for another PR.

## Follow-up

The rename sweep across the docs (about 110 mentions in 7 pages) waits for the open docs PRs on those pages to land, to avoid conflicts: #904, #862, #866, #863, #878, #906, #918, #861, #850, #911, #923. Code docstrings, error messages and examples (about 300 mentions) come in a separate PR.

pull_requests.title: feat(temporal): unchecked_args for framework arguments that grant nothing
pull_requests.body:
Adds `TenuoPluginConfig.unchecked_args`: activity parameter names that are left out of PoP signing and the warrant check. Some frameworks pass every activity an extra argument of their own (for example a pydantic context object saying where to publish events) and dispatch activities by name. Today that argument fails PoP normalization, so every call fails closed, and under closed-world constraints a warrant would have to name it. With `unchecked_args={"tool_ctx"}`, that argument is skipped and every other argument is checked as before.

An unchecked argument isn't covered by the PoP, so only arguments that grant nothing should be listed; the docstring and `docs/temporal-reference.md` say so. As an extra check alongside PoP, a worker with the setting on names arguments from the activity function's own signature and denies a call whose `x-tenuo-arg-keys` header disagrees or whose function isn't available. That means activities dispatched by name need to be in `activity_fns` once the setting is on. Behaviour is unchanged when it's off.

Tested with a live-server suite (`tests/e2e/test_temporal_unchecked_args.py`): a pydantic context argument with by-name dispatch fails closed without the setting, runs with it (the activity still receives the context), out-of-scope arguments are still denied, and a relabelled header is denied. Removing the worker-side drop, the signature check, or the full-name header each fails a test. The existing Temporal suites pass (500).

pull_requests.title: Make Tenuo onboarding skills version-aware and testable
pull_requests.body:
## Related Issue

Closes #954. Related historical work: #672.

## Summary

Developers asking an agent to secure their project need guidance that matches the installed Tenuo runtime and actual effect boundary. This makes local SDK or supported CLI onboarding the default: inspect the project, propose useful task authority and key ownership, implement a supported integration, and demonstrate allowed execution and denied calls with zero effects. Existing Cloud workflows and a staged move to managed issuance are supported without making Cloud a prerequisite.

- Separate installed runtime, matching release, merged main and pending PR hazards. Add a refreshable inventory of every open Daniel/Niki PR with reviewed impact, dependencies and framework status.
- Add real OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, Temporal and MCP dispatch regressions, exact native-build provenance, heuristic scanners and separate structural/freshness/behavioral readiness levels.
- Add one-command released-SDK examples for five framework paths: an approved invoice payment succeeds while bank diversion, another invoice and an excessive delegated amount are refused. No model key, Cloud account or real payment.
- Correct warrant/audit guidance around runtime API availability, trusted roots, chain/PoP evidence, unknown arguments and review-versus-implementation routing. Preserve exact historical coding-agent inputs and failures.

## Test Plan

- [x] 72 script unit tests; structural/release-pin validation and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] 38 freshly rebuilt-main real-framework cases pass: OpenAI 7, LangGraph 10, live Temporal 7, MCP 1 and MCP 2 7 each.
- [x] 8 quickstart test methods pass, including all five one-command real-framework demonstrations; each proves one allowed effect and three constraint denials with zero effects.
- [x] Actual warrant Markdown example/released Python probes: 11 pass; installed TypeScript diagnostics: 5 pass.
- [x] Independently built local CLI PR951 leaf `ebdfb291`: 89 focused cases and 3 live Temporal cases pass. Independent CLI issuance → LangChain allow/deny workflow passes. Later `cb440d2` default-workspace delta was inspected separately; the executed tests apply only to the named older leaf.
- [x] Latest reviewed snapshot inventories 124 open author PRs; online freshness remains a separate check.
- [x] Earlier seven-project coding-agent round and 23-case project-onboarding diagnostic passed against their preserved older skill inputs. Subsequent edits leave this evidence stale; it is not silently renewed.
- [ ] Finish fresh payment/framework/onboarding and routing evaluations against final guidance. Distribution readiness remains **NOT READY**.
- [ ] Full `./scripts/check.sh` and live Cloud service migration are not claimed as tested.

This draft supports continued review and testing; it is not distribution/promotion approval. Marketplace/plugin publication is outside this PR. See `tests/agent-skills/tenuo-agent-authorization/handoff.md` and `audit.md` for current evidence and remaining work.

## Security Invariants

- [x] No core verifier, adapter runtime or wire-format behavior is rewritten. Examples use the resolved Rust-backed SDK; generic effect-service recipes do not certify every official adapter.
- [x] Denied-path tests assert zero protected effect invocations. Setup errors or exceptions after an effect do not qualify.
- [x] Guidance requires independently configured roots, complete delegated chains, holder-key separation and authority that can only narrow. Pending PR APIs are not installed functionality.
- [x] Observe decisions are distinct from blocked effects. Per-call authorization is not cumulative accounting, replay prevention, idempotency, process isolation or downstream completion.
- [x] Evaluation artifacts use fake effects and disposable development keys. Private Cloud source, provider/model credentials and real payments are not included.
